docs.gettingStarted.page: The package has two entry points, and the second one is the renderer:
import { node, add, mount, Bounded, Surfaced } from "game-kit"
They are separate because `pixi.js` reaches for a canvas context as soon as it is imported.
Re-exporting the painter from the main entry would pull WebGL into every consumer, including
rules running on a server and every headless test.
import { node, mount, attachPainter, installStockSurfaces, installStockLayouts } from "game-kit"
installStockSurfaces()   // the named records a surface can point at
installStockLayouts()    // the named arrangements a container can ask for
`mount` is the host: it takes a DOM element to live in, creates the view inside it, measures
the viewport and watches it for resizes. Nothing is on screen yet — no atom here paints.
`Bounded` is the box: a hit area, a silhouette, a place in the owner's layout. It draws
nothing. `Surfaced` is what draws, and it needs an area — from the node's own box or from the
extent of its content, which is how a desk can have a surface and no box of its own.
A surface is a reference to a registered record, not a set of colours on the node:
node("ace", Bounded({ bounds: { kind: "rect", w: 1, h: 1.4 } }), Surfaced({ surface: "cardFace" }))
Re-register the record and every card changes at once, while no box moves. The name is also
what travels between clients — one short string instead of a palette copied into every message.
A node holds children without `Container`; the atom decides how they are arranged. `free`
places nobody, so each child keeps the pose it was given, and `row` places everyone. Register
your own with `registerLayout` — spacing and the like are parameters of the record, not fields
You give a node its id. The same node is read from several places — another player's device, a
save reopened tomorrow — and a counter hidden inside `node()` would be unique in one tab and
nowhere else. When ids disagree, a move does not fail; it lands on a different existing node.
Ids come from the spec for authored nodes (`board`, `hand`, `discard`), and from the world's

No rules, no turn order, no networking, no dragging. What exists is the ladder in the sidebar
and the machinery under it. To find the edge, open the atoms and read what each one claims —
every claim on those pages has a test behind it.
